qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals issued by the City of Providence for parking signs and related materials, including submission deadlines, scope of work, and evaluation criteria.

quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS
Date to be opened: 7/27/2026

The City of Providence Department of Public Works, Parking Administration Division, seeks competitive bids from qualified manufacturers and distributors for the furnishing and delivery of parking regulatory signs, parking sign posts, mounting hardware, parking control devices, and related materials on an as-needed basis under a firm fixed unit price requirements contract.

Award shall be made to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder based on the aggregate evaluated price and the bidder's demonstrated responsibility, delivery capability, product quality, warranty, references, and compliance with the specifications.
Bids may be submitted up to 2:15 P.M. on the above meeting date at the Department of the City Clerk.

findings.title: Proof of Insurance and Good Standing Required
findings.fact: Bidders must be able to provide proof of insurance and a Certificate of Good Standing with the Rhode Island Secretary of State upon request.

quotes.quote: You must be able to provide: • Business Tax ID will be requested after an award is approved by the Board of Contract and Supply. • Proof of Insurance. • Certificate of Good Standing with the Rhode Island Secretary of State.

findings.title: No Pre-Bid Conference Scheduled
findings.fact: There is no pre-bid conference scheduled for this item.

quotes.quote: Pre-submission Conference There is no pre-bid conference scheduled for this item.

findings.title: Evaluation of Optional Installation Services
findings.fact: Pricing for installation services is evaluated separately from the base bid and does not affect determination of lowest bidder for materials.

quotes.quote: Pricing for installation services shall be evaluated separately from the base bid and shall not affect the determination of the lowest responsive and responsible bidder for the materials portion of the solicitation unless otherwise stated in the Bid Form.

findings.title: Estimated Quantities for Bid Evaluation
findings.fact: Estimated quantities are provided solely for bid evaluation and are not guaranteed.

quotes.quote: Estimated quantities are provided solely for bid evaluation.

findings.title: Right to Request Additional Information
findings.fact: The City reserves the right to request clarifications, product literature, samples, and additional information prior to award.

quotes.quote: The City reserves the right to request clarifications, product literature, samples, and additional information prior to award, waive minor informalities, reject any or all bids, and determine the bid most advantageous to the City.

findings.title: Cash Discounts Not Considered
findings.fact: In determining the lowest responsible bidder, cash discounts based on preferable payment terms will not be considered.

quotes.quote: In determining the lowest responsible bidder, cash discounts based on preferable payment terms will not be considered.

findings.title: Equal Prices May Be Split or Awarded to One Bidder
findings.fact: Where prices are the same, the Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to award to one bidder, or to split the award.

quotes.quote: Where prices are the same, the Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to award to one bidder, or to split the award.

findings.title: Equal in Quality Basis
findings.fact: Bids may be submitted on an 'equal in quality' basis. The City reserves the right to decide equality.

quotes.quote: Bids may be submitted on an “equal in quality” basis. The City reserves the right to decide equality.

findings.title: Unit Price Governs in Case of Error
findings.fact: In case of error in the extension of prices quoted, the unit price will govern.

quotes.quote: In case of error in the extension of prices quoted, the unit price will govern.

findings.title: Renewal Price Adjustment Cap
findings.fact: Renewal price adjustments are limited to the lesser of CPI-U increase or 3%.

quotes.quote: Renewal price adjustments may be requested only during renewal periods and shall not exceed the lesser of the annual CPI-U increase or three percent, supported by documentation.

findings.title: Tax Exemption
findings.fact: Prices quoted shall not include Federal Excise Taxes or Rhode Island Sales Tax.

quotes.quote: As the City of Providence is exempt from the payment of Federal Excise Taxes and Rhode Island Sales Tax, prices quoted are not to include these taxes.

findings.title: No Assignment Without Consent
findings.fact: Contractor cannot assign or underlet the contract without prior written consent of the City Purchasing Director.

quotes.quote: The contractor will NOT be permitted to: a) assign or underlet the contract, or b) assign either legally or equitably any monies or any claim thereto without the previous written consent of the City Purchasing Director.

findings.title: Delivery Dates Must Be Shown
findings.fact: Bidders must specify delivery dates; otherwise immediate delivery from stock is assumed.

quotes.quote: Delivery dates must be shown in the bid. If no delivery date is specified, it will be assumed that an immediate delivery from stock will be made.

findings.title: No Goods Without Purchase Order
findings.fact: No goods should be delivered or work started without a Purchase Order.

quotes.quote: No goods should be delivered, or work started without a Purchase Order.

findings.title: No Interest on Overdue Invoices
findings.fact: The City shall not be obligated to pay interest on any overdue invoice or payment.

quotes.quote: In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay or shall you be entitled to receive interest on any overdue invoice or payment.

findings.title: No Collection Costs
findings.fact: The City shall not be obligated to pay any costs associated with your collection of an outstanding invoice.

quotes.quote: In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay any costs associated with your collection of an outstanding invoice.

findings.title: No Partial Payment for Commodities
findings.fact: Payment for partial delivery will not be allowed except when provided for in blanket or term contracts.

quotes.quote: Payment for partial delivery will not be allowed except when provided for in blanket or term contracts.

findings.title: Single Shipping Charge for Partial Deliveries
findings.fact: Only one shipping charge will be applied in the event of partial deliveries for blanket or term contracts.

quotes.quote: Only one shipping charge will be applied in the event of partial deliveries for blanket or term contracts.

findings.title: Annual Costs for Contracts Exceeding 12 Months
findings.fact: Contracts exceeding twelve months must specify annual costs for each year.

quotes.quote: Contracts exceeding twelve months must specify annual costs for each year.

findings.title: Bids Should Be Totaled
findings.fact: Bids should be totaled so that the final cost is clearly stated, unless submitting a unit price bid.

quotes.quote: Bids SHOULD BE TOTALED so that the final cost is clearly stated (unless submitting a unit price bid), however each item should be priced individually.

findings.title: Awards May Be by Total or Individual Items
findings.fact: Awards may be made on the basis of total bid or by individual items.

quotes.quote: Awards may be made on the basis of total bid or by individual items.

findings.title: No Automatic Renewal
findings.fact: The Agreement shall not automatically renew or be extended without a writing signed by the parties.

quotes.quote: In no event shall the Agreement automatically renew or be extended without a writing signed by the parties.

findings.title: No Assignment Without Consent
findings.fact: You shall not assign your rights and obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the City.

quotes.quote: You shall not assign your rights and obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the City.

findings.title: Independent Contractor Status
findings.fact: You are an independent contractor and not an employee or agent of the City, and the City shall not deduct taxes.

quotes.quote: You are an independent contractor and in no way does this Agreement render you an employee or agent of the City or entitle you to fringe benefits, workers’ compensation, pension obligations, retirement or any other employment benefits. The City shall not deduct federal or state income taxes, social security or Medicare withholdings, or any other taxes required to be deducted by an employer, and this is your responsibility to yourself and your employees and agents.

findings.title: Five Years Experience and Three Municipal References Required
findings.fact: Bidder must have at least five years of experience manufacturing traffic control signs and provide three municipal references demonstrating comparable work.
findings.business_implication: This is a mandatory qualification. Bidders without the required experience and references will be disqualified. It ensures the City only considers vendors with proven capability.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your company meets the five-year experience requirement and prepare documentation for three municipal references. If you lack the experience, consider partnering with a qualified manufacturer or subcontractor, but ensure compliance with the solicitation's requirements.

quotes.quote: Bidder shall have at least five years of experience manufacturing traffic control signs and provide three municipal references demonstrating comparable work.

findings.title: Out-of-State Corporation Must Register in Rhode Island
findings.fact: A bidder who is an out-of-state corporation shall qualify or register to transact business in Rhode Island in accordance with the Rhode Island Business Corporation Act.
findings.business_implication: Out-of-state corporations must be authorized to do business in Rhode Island before bidding. Failure to do so could result in disqualification or legal issues.
findings.action_recommendation: If your company is incorporated outside Rhode Island, ensure you are registered or qualified to transact business in the state. Obtain the necessary certificates and include them in your bid package.

quotes.quote: A bidder who is an out-of-state corporation shall qualify or register to transact business in this State, in accordance with the Rhode Island Business Corporation Act, RIGL Sec. 7-1.2-1401, et seq.

findings.title: Bidder Must Not Discriminate and Must Comply with Hiring Laws
findings.fact: Bidder must certify that it does not unlawfully discriminate and that all employees are lawfully employed under applicable laws.
findings.business_implication: This certification is a legal requirement. Non-compliance with anti-discrimination and employment laws could lead to disqualification, penalties, or contract termination.
findings.action_recommendation: Review your company's hiring practices to ensure compliance with all applicable laws. Complete and sign the required certification (Bid Form 2) and be prepared to provide evidence of compliance if requested.

quotes.quote: Bidder must certify that it does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation and/or religion in its business and hiring practices and that all of its employees are lawfully employed under all applicable federal, state and local laws, rules and regulations. (See Bid Form 2.)

findings.title: Bidder Must Provide Local Agent for Service of Process if Out-of-State
findings.fact: If the bidder's company is based in a state other than Rhode Island, it must list name and contact information for a local agent for service of process located within Rhode Island.
findings.business_implication: Out-of-state bidders must have a local agent in Rhode Island to receive legal documents. This is a legal requirement for doing business in the state.
findings.action_recommendation: If your company is based outside Rhode Island, designate a local agent for service of process and provide their name and contact information in the bid form. Ensure the agent is willing to accept service on your behalf.

quotes.quote: If the bidder’s company is based in a state other than Rhode Island, list name and contact information for a local agent for service of process that is located within Rhode Island

findings.title: Disqualification for Submitting Sensitive Information Directly to Issuing Department
findings.fact: Bidders who submit sensitive information directly to the issuing department to protect pricing terms from becoming public will be disqualified.
findings.business_implication: This is a strict rule to maintain transparency. Attempting to bypass the official submission process will result in immediate disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Do not submit any information directly to the issuing department unless specifically requested. Submit all required documents through the official channels (e.g., City Clerk) as instructed. If you have concerns about sensitive information, follow the proper procedures for redaction or request guidance from the purchasing department.

quotes.quote: Bidders who make such an attempt will be disqualified.

findings.title: Disqualification for Failure to Provide Supplemental Information
findings.fact: Failure to provide supplemental information requested by the issuing department may lead to disqualification of the bid.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to provide additional documentation (e.g., Business Tax ID, Proof of Insurance, Certificate of Good Standing) upon request after being selected as the best-suited bidder. Failure to provide these items can result in disqualification, even if the bid was initially successful.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all required supplemental documents are readily available and up-to-date before bid submission. Designate a point of contact to respond promptly to any requests from the issuing department.

quotes.quote: An inability to provide the outlined items at the request of the department may lead to the disqualification of your bid.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Waiver Form Required for Award Recommendation
findings.fact: City Department Directors should not recommend a bidder for an award if the MBE/WBE waiver form is not included, absent, or not signed by the MBE/WBE director.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder does not meet the 20% MBE/WBE participation goal, they must submit a waiver request form that is properly signed by the MBE/WBE Outreach Director. Without this, the bidder cannot be recommended for award, potentially losing the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: If the MBE/WBE participation goal is not met, complete the waiver request form and submit it to the MBE/WBE Outreach Director for signature before bid submission. Ensure the signed form is included in the bid package.

quotes.quote: In case a waiver is needed, City Department Directors should not recommend a bidder for an award if this form is not included, absent or is not signed by the city of Providence MBE/WBE director.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Certification Required at Time of Bid
findings.fact: All MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers must be certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that any MBE/WBE subcontractors or suppliers listed in the bid are certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid submission. If they are not certified, the bid may be considered non-responsive or disqualified.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify the certification status of all MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers before bid submission. Use the City's MBE/WBE Directory to confirm certification and maintain documentation of certification.

quotes.quote: Please note that all MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers must be certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid.

findings.title: Apprentice Requirements for Construction Projects
findings.fact: Construction projects valued at $100,000 or more must utilize not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.
findings.business_implication: For construction projects over $100,000, the bidder must allocate at least 15% of total work hours to apprentices. Non-compliance may result in payment delays or penalties. The bidder must also report compliance with payment requisitions.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan workforce allocation to meet the 15% apprentice hour requirement. Prepare to submit compliance reports with each payment requisition and attend the mandatory meeting post-award to understand specific documentation requirements.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for utilizing not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.

findings.title: First Source Requirements for Construction Projects
findings.fact: Construction projects must comply with the City's First Source Ordinance requiring hiring Providence residents.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must make a good faith effort to hire Providence residents for the project. Failure to comply may result in payment delays or penalties. The bidder must report hiring efforts and progress with payment requisitions.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a plan to recruit and hire Providence residents. Keep detailed records of hiring efforts and outcomes. Submit compliance reports with each payment requisition and attend the mandatory post-award meeting to understand specific requirements.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for hiring Providence residents to work on this project.

findings.title: Deadline for Questions
findings.fact: Questions must be submitted via email by July 20, 2026 at 4:00 PM (EST).
findings.business_implication: This is the last opportunity to clarify any ambiguities in the RFP before bid submission. Missing this deadline could result in misunderstandings and a non-compliant bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP thoroughly and submit all questions via email to purchasing@providenceri.gov with the subject line 'Solicitation Question' before the deadline. Keep a record of all questions and responses.

quotes.quote: Deadline for questions submissions: via email by July 20, 2026 at 4:00 PM (EST).

findings.title: Award within 90 days of bid opening
findings.fact: Awards will be made within ninety (90) days of bid opening.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to maintain pricing and availability for at least 90 days after bid opening. Any changes in costs or supply could impact profitability if the award is delayed.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that pricing remains valid for at least 90 days and have contingency plans for potential cost increases or supply chain disruptions during this period.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made within nighty (90) days of bid opening.

findings.title: Bid opening date referenced on page 1
findings.fact: The bid opening date is noted on page 1 of the RFP.
findings.business_implication: The bid opening date is the deadline for bid submission. Missing this date will result in disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Note the bid opening date (7/27/2026) and ensure that the bid is submitted to the City Clerk's office before that date. Plan internal timelines to complete all required forms and documentation well in advance.

quotes.quote: This information is NOT requested to be provided in your initial bid that you will submit to the City Clerk’s office by the “date to be opened” noted on page 1.

findings.title: Lowest Responsive and Responsible Bidder
findings.fact: Award shall be made to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder based on aggregate evaluated price and other factors.
findings.business_implication: The award is not solely based on price; the city will also consider responsibility, delivery capability, product quality, warranty, references, and compliance. A low bid may not win if other factors are not satisfactory.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the bid demonstrates strong capabilities in all evaluation criteria. Provide detailed information on delivery schedules, product quality, warranties, and references. Highlight any relevant experience and compliance with specifications.

quotes.quote: Award shall be made to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder based on the aggregate evaluated price and the bidder's demonstrated responsibility, delivery capability, product quality, warranty, references, and compliance with the specifications.

findings.title: Award to Lowest Qualified and Responsible Bidder
findings.fact: The Board of Contract and Supply will make the award to the lowest qualified and responsible bidder.
findings.business_implication: The Board has the discretion to determine which bidder is 'qualified and responsible.' This means that even if a bidder is the lowest price, they may not be awarded if they are not deemed responsible or qualified.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare to demonstrate financial stability, past performance, and technical capability. Be ready to provide any requested documentation, such as financial statements, references, and certifications, to prove responsibility and qualification.

quotes.quote: The Board of Contract and Supply will make the award to the lowest qualified and responsible bidder.

findings.title: Right to Reject Any and All Bids
findings.fact: The Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to reject any and all bids.
findings.business_implication: The City has broad discretion to reject all bids, meaning even a compliant and competitive bid may not be accepted. This introduces uncertainty into the bidding process and could result in no award being made.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should ensure their bid is fully compliant and competitive, but also be aware that the City may reject all bids. It is advisable to clarify any ambiguities in the RFP before submission and to prepare for the possibility that the contract may not be awarded.

quotes.quote: The Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to reject any and all bids.

findings.title: Supplemental Information May Be Requested for Best Suited Bid
findings.fact: If the issuing department determines that a firm's bid is best suited, the firm will be asked to provide proof of certain items prior to formalizing an award.
findings.business_implication: Even if a bidder is the apparent best fit, the award is not final until supplemental information is provided and approved. Failure to provide these items in a timely manner could lead to disqualification, even if the bid was initially selected.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should prepare all required supplemental documents (e.g., Business Tax ID, Proof of Insurance, Certificate of Good Standing) in advance so they can be submitted promptly upon request. Ensure these documents are current and readily available to avoid delays or disqualification.

quotes.quote: If the issuing department for this RFP determines that your firm’s bid is best suited to accommodate their need, you will be asked to provide proof of the following prior to formalizing an award.

findings.title: Firm Fixed Unit Price Contract
findings.fact: The contract is a firm fixed unit price contract with prices firm for the initial term, subject to renewal adjustments.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must commit to fixed unit prices for the entire initial contract term, which could be up to one year. This means the bidder bears the risk of cost increases (e.g., materials, labor, freight) during that period. However, renewal terms may allow for price adjustments, providing some flexibility.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should carefully estimate all costs, including potential increases in materials, labor, and freight, to ensure the fixed prices remain profitable. Consider including a contingency in the pricing to mitigate risks. Also, review the renewal price adjustment mechanism to understand how future price changes will be handled.

quotes.quote: The Contractor shall provide all awarded items at the fixed unit prices submitted in its bid for the duration of the initial contract term. Unit prices shall include all labor, materials, manufacturing, packaging, freight, delivery, overhead, profit, and all other costs necessary to furnish the requested items. Except as otherwise provided for approved renewal-term price adjustments, unit prices shall remain firm throughout the contract term.

findings.title: Payment Terms: 60 Days
findings.fact: Invoices submitted to the City shall be payable sixty (60) days from the time of receipt by the City.
findings.business_implication: The City will pay invoices 60 days after receipt, which may create cash flow challenges for the bidder, especially if the bidder has to pay suppliers or employees before receiving payment. The City also does not pay interest on overdue invoices, so late payments do not incur penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should assess their cash flow and ensure they have sufficient working capital to cover expenses during the 60-day payment period. Consider factoring in the cost of financing into the bid price. Also, ensure that invoices are complete and include all required documentation to avoid delays in payment processing.

quotes.quote: Invoices submitted to the City shall be payable sixty (60) days from the time of receipt by the City.

findings.title: Firm Prices for 90 Days
findings.fact: All bid prices will be considered firm for 90 days after bid opening, and requests for price increases will not be honored.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must hold its prices for at least 90 days after bid opening, even if the award is delayed. This means the bidder cannot adjust prices to reflect cost increases during this period, which could impact profitability if costs rise unexpectedly.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should ensure their bid prices are valid for at least 90 days and include a buffer for potential cost increases. Monitor market conditions and factor in potential price volatility when preparing the bid. Avoid submitting bids with prices that are only viable for a short period.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made within nighty (90) days of bid opening. All bid prices will be considered firm, unless qualified otherwise. Requests for price increases will not be honored.

findings.title: Bid Prices in Writing and Figures
findings.fact: Bid prices must be stated both in writing and in figures, and proposals not so stated may be rejected.
findings.business_implication: Failure to state prices in both formats could lead to automatic rejection of the bid, regardless of the competitiveness of the price.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the bid form clearly states the total amount in both written words and numerical figures. Double-check for consistency between the two formats before submission.

quotes.quote: The price or prices proposed should be stated both in WRITING and in FIGURES, and any proposal not so stated may be rejected.

findings.title: Entire Agreement Clause
findings.fact: The RFP and Standard Terms and Conditions together constitute the entire agreement, and they supersede any conflicting provisions in the bid.
findings.business_implication: Any additional terms or conditions included in the bid will be disregarded if they conflict with the RFP or Standard Terms, potentially exposing the bidder to unintended obligations.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review the RFP and Standard Terms to ensure that the bid does not contain any conflicting provisions. If exceptions are necessary, clearly note them as exceptions and be prepared for them to be rejected.

quotes.quote: The Request For Proposals (“RFP”) and these Standard Terms and Conditions together constitute the entire agreement of the parties (“the Agreement”) with regard to any and all matters. By your submission of a bid proposal or response to the City’s RFP, you accept these Standard Terms & Conditions and agree that they supersede any conflicting provisions provided by bid or in any terms and conditions contained or linked within a bid and/or response.

findings.title: Prevailing Wage and First Source Apply
findings.fact: For construction contracts, applicable state labor law concerning prevailing wage rates and the City’s First Source Ordinance apply.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must comply with prevailing wage requirements and the First Source Ordinance, which may increase labor costs and impose hiring obligations, affecting the bid price and workforce planning.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the impact of prevailing wage rates and First Source hiring requirements on the bid. Ensure that the bid price accounts for these costs and that the company can meet the hiring obligations.

quotes.quote: For contracts involving construction, alteration, and/or repair work, the provisions of applicable state labor law concerning payment of prevailing wage rates (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 37-13-1 et seq., as amended) and the City’s First Source Ordinance (Providence Code of Ordinances §§ 21-91 et seq., as amended) apply.

findings.title: Governing Law and Venue
findings.fact: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Rhode Island, and any actions shall occur solely in Rhode Island state or federal court.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to litigate any disputes in Rhode Island, which may be inconvenient and costly if the bidder is located elsewhere, and must understand that Rhode Island law will apply.
findings.action_recommendation: Evaluate the implications of the governing law and venue clause. If the bidder is not familiar with Rhode Island law, consider consulting legal counsel. Ensure that the bidder is willing to accept this jurisdiction.

quotes.quote: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Rhode Island. You expressly submit yourself to and agree that any and all actions arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the Agreement or relationship between the parties shall occur solely in the venue and jurisdiction of the State of Rhode Island or the federal court located in Rhode Island.

findings.title: Unlimited Indemnification Obligation
findings.fact: The contractor must indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City from any and all claims, damages, losses, etc., arising out of the performance of the work, with no stated limitation.
findings.business_implication: The bidder could face unlimited liability for claims arising from the work, including legal fees, which could be financially devastating and may not be fully covered by insurance.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully assess the risks and ensure that adequate insurance coverage is in place. Consider negotiating for a limitation of liability or a cap on indemnification, though the City may not accept such changes. Consult with legal counsel to understand the full extent of the obligation.

quotes.quote: To the fullest extent permitted by law, you shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City, its employees, officers, agents, and assigns from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, allegations, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, obligations, fines, penalties, judgments, liabilities, costs and expenses, including but not limited to attorneys’ fees, of any nature whatsoever arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement.

findings.title: No Limitation of Liability
findings.fact: The City does not agree to limit the contractor's liability to the contract price or any other monetary limit, and the City retains the full statute of limitations to bring claims.
findings.business_implication: The contractor faces unlimited liability exposure for any claims arising from the contract, with no cap on damages. This could lead to significant financial risk, especially for large or complex projects.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the potential risks and consider obtaining comprehensive insurance coverage, including professional liability and excess liability, to mitigate the financial impact. Also, consider negotiating for a mutual waiver of consequential damages or a reasonable liability cap, though the City may be unwilling to concede.

quotes.quote: The City shall not subject itself to any contractual limitations on liability. The City shall have the time permitted within the applicable statute of limitations, and no less, to bring or assert any and all causes of action, suits, claims or demands the City may have arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement, and in no event does the City agree to limit your liability to the price of the Agreement or any other monetary limit.

findings.title: Mandatory Insurance and Additional Insured
findings.fact: The contractor must maintain insurance coverage and name the City as an additional insured on general liability and umbrella policies.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must secure and maintain specific insurance policies, which may increase costs. Naming the City as an additional insured extends coverage to the City, potentially increasing the contractor's insurance premiums and administrative burden.
findings.action_recommendation: Review current insurance policies to ensure they meet the requirements and can accommodate the City as an additional insured. Obtain quotes from insurers to understand the cost implications and ensure compliance before signing the contract.

quotes.quote: You shall maintain throughout the term of this Agreement the insurance coverage that is required by the RFP or, if none is required in the RFP, insurance coverage that is considered in your industry to be commercially reasonable, and you agree to name the City as an additional insured on your general liability policy and on any umbrella policy you carry.

findings.title: Data Breach Notification and Liability
findings.fact: The contractor must comply with data protection laws, implement security measures, and notify the City within 24 hours of a breach, with potential liability for breaches.
findings.business_implication: The contractor assumes significant responsibility for data protection and faces strict notification deadlines. Non-compliance could lead to legal penalties, reputational damage, and financial liability for breaches.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust data security measures, including encryption, access controls, and employee training. Establish a breach response plan that ensures notification to the City within 24 hours. Consider obtaining cyber liability insurance to cover potential costs.

quotes.quote: For any Agreement involving the sharing or exchange of data involving potentially confidential and/or personal information, you shall comply with any and all state and/or federal laws or regulations applicable to confidential and/or personal information you receive from the City, including but not limited to the Rhode Island Identity Theft Protection Act, R.I. Gen. Laws § 11-49.3-1, during the term of the Agreement. You shall implement and maintain appropriate physical, technical, and administrative security measures for the protection of, and to prevent access to, use, or disclosure of, confidential and/or personal information. In the event of a breach of such information, you shall notify the City of such breach immediately, but in no event later than twenty-four (24) hours after discovery of such breach.

findings.title: No Dispute Resolution or Arbitration
findings.fact: The City is not required to submit to dispute resolution or mandatory/binding arbitration, limiting the contractor's options for resolving disputes.
findings.business_implication: The contractor may be forced to litigate disputes in court, which can be time-consuming and costly. The lack of alternative dispute resolution mechanisms reduces flexibility and may disadvantage the contractor.
findings.action_recommendation: Before signing, consider whether the dispute resolution clause is acceptable. If possible, negotiate for a mutual agreement to use mediation or non-binding arbitration. Alternatively, ensure that the contract's governing law and venue are favorable and that you have legal counsel prepared for potential litigation.

quotes.quote: With regard to any issues, claims, or controversies that may arise under this Agreement, the City shall not be required to submit to dispute resolution or mandatory/binding arbitration.

findings.title: No Waiver of Rights
findings.fact: The City's failure to enforce any provision does not waive its rights, and a waiver of one breach does not waive subsequent breaches.
findings.business_implication: The contractor cannot rely on the City's past inaction as a defense for future non-compliance. The City retains the right to enforce any provision at any time, which may create uncertainty.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure strict compliance with all contract terms at all times, as the City may enforce any provision at its discretion. Maintain thorough documentation of all communications and performance to demonstrate compliance.

quotes.quote: The failure of the City to require performance of any provision shall not affect the City’s right to require performance at any time thereafter, nor shall a waiver of any breach or default of this Agreement constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach or default or a waiver of the provision itself.

findings.title: Termination for Default Due to Failure to Deliver or Meet Specifications
findings.fact: Failure to deliver within the time quoted or failure to meet specifications may result in default in accordance with the general specifications.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure timely delivery and strict compliance with specifications to avoid being declared in default, which could lead to termination of the contract and potential liability for damages.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the delivery schedule and specifications carefully. Develop a robust project management plan to ensure on-time delivery and quality compliance. Consider including contingency buffers for potential delays.

quotes.quote: Failure to deliver within the time quoted or failure to meet specifications may result in default in accordance with the general specifications.

findings.title: Conflicting Requirements for Financial Assurance
findings.fact: Page 10 states that financial assurance is required only if specified on page 12, but page 12 provides checkboxes for financial assurance options and states that if either of the first two checkboxes is checked, the specified assurance must accompany the bid. However, the actual checkboxes are not marked, creating ambiguity about whether financial assurance is required for this solicitation.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity regarding financial assurance requirements creates uncertainty for the bidder. If the bidder fails to provide required financial assurance, the bid may be rejected. Conversely, providing unnecessary financial assurance could tie up capital unnecessarily.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from the purchasing department before bid submission. If clarification is not possible, consider including a conditional financial assurance (e.g., a bid bond) to cover potential requirements, or prepare to provide assurance if requested. Document all communications regarding this ambiguity.

quotes.quote: Financial Assurance, if requested (as indicated on page 5 of this document under “Bid Terms”) All of the above listed documents are REQUIRED. (With the exception of financial assurances, which are only required if specified on page 12.)

Financial assurances may be required in order to be a successful bidder for Commodity or Construction and Service contracts. If either of the first two checkboxes below is checked, the specified assurance must accompany a bid, or the bid will not be considered by the Board of Contract and Supply. The third checkbox indicates the lowest responsible bidder will be contacted and required to post a bond to be awarded the contract. a) A certified check for $ must be deposited with the City Clerk as a guarantee that the Contract will be signed and delivered by the bidder. b) A bid bond in the amount of per centum (%) of the proposed total price, must be deposited with the City Clerk as a guarantee that the contract will be signed and delivered by the bidder; and the amount of such bid bond shall be retained for the use of the City as liquidated damages in case of default. Any person signing a bid bond as an attorney-in-fact shall include with the bid bond an original, or a photocopy or facsimile of an original, power of attorney. c) A performance and payment bond with a satisfactory surety company will be posted by the bidder in a sum equal to one hundred per centum (100%) of the awarded contract. d) No financial assurance is necessary for this item.

findings.title: Conflicting Requirements for Installation Services
findings.fact: Page 4 states that installation services are optional and may be awarded to the same contractor as the materials contract, but page 4 also states that installation services shall not be included in the base bid and shall only be performed when specifically authorized. However, page 4 also states that the City may elect not to award the installation portion at all. This creates ambiguity about whether installation services are a separate contract or an optional add-on to the materials contract.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity around installation services may affect bid pricing and resource allocation. If the bidder assumes installation is included but it is not, they may underprice. Conversely, if they assume it is separate, they may miss out on potential revenue.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with the City whether installation services will be a separate contract or an optional add-on. If unclear, prepare a base bid for materials only and provide separate pricing for installation services as an option. Ensure that the bid clearly states that installation is not included in the base bid unless specifically requested.

quotes.quote: At the City's option, the Contractor may also provide sign installation services as described in Section 7A (Optional Add/Alternate Sign Installation Services). Installation services shall not be included in the base bid and shall only be performed when specifically authorized by the City through a purchase order or work authorization.
The City may, at its sole discretion, award the installation portion of this solicitation to the same contractor awarded the materials contract or may elect not to award this portion at all.
